newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Jakarta call money traded at 5.5/6.0 percent.
newsitem.headline: Jakarta call money traded at 5.5/6.0 percent.

text.p: Jakarta call money was traded at 5.5/6.0 percent on Thursday morning on ample liquidity, dealers said.

One state bank dealer said the condition had not changed much from the past few days as the central bank was keeping the market flush to enable operators to prepare for higher tax payments and meet the new reserve requirement rate of five percent.
One-week money was at 6.75 percent and two-week at 8.5 percent, while the one-month money was traded at around the bilateral central bank paper rate of 10.75 points.
The central bank kept its bilateral rates stable. It offered seven-day SBIs at 6.5 percent, 14-day at 8.5 percent and one-month at 10.75 percent.
The average overnight interbank rate on Wednesday was 7.11 percent, compared with 8.25 percent on Tuesday.
Bond dealers said the market remained strong, with prices seen little changed in the morning.
One said Mulialand was well bid. It was last traded at around 108 percent, which gave a yield of some 15.78 percent.
The yield of the benchmark PLN V/A bond was at around 15.0 percent on a price of 107.25 percent.
